hero.tagline: Where moonlit silver meets the endless tide of thought

today.heading: The moonlit garden blooms in silence, yet speaks volumes to those who pause.

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Chandra's quiet dominion
moon.intro: The Moon controls the tides of the ocean and the tides of the mind. In Vedic thought, Chandra governs the Manas — the emotional mind — and its phases mirror the cycles of human desire and detachment.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: The ego: a wave believing itself alone
philosophy.intro: In the ocean of existence, arrogance is a wave that believes it is separate from the sea. It rises, it crashes, and it returns — never having been anything but water.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: The soul that cannot be slain
gita.intro: The Gita describes the soul as 'unborn, eternal, ever-existing, undying, and primeval.' It is not slain when the body is slain. This is not metaphor — it is the foundational axiom of Hindu philosophy.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Shiva plays the damaru of creation
shiva.intro: The Shiv Purana describes the damaru — Shiva's drum — as the source of all language and music. The first sound, Nada, is the vibration from which all creation emerges. Music is not entertainment; it is cosmology.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Beauty: the impermanent made eternal
art.intro: The Japanese concept of 'wabi-sabi' finds beauty in imperfection — the cracked pot, the weathered stone, the fading flower. It teaches that transience is not the enemy of beauty but its essence.
